By the (angels) who pull out (the souls of the disbelievers) with violence, (wa-l-nazi'at): ﴿By those who drag forth with violence﴾, that is, the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers, pulling them out with great force (gharqan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 2:

﴿And by those who draw out gently﴾ — the angels who draw out the souls of the believers, that is, they extract them gently.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 79, verse 3:

﴿وَالسَّابِحَاتِ سَبْحًا﴾ The angels swim from the sky by His command, may He be exalted, i.e., they descend.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 4:

﴿By those who race in a race﴾: the angels race with the souls of the believers to Paradise.

﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾: the angels, who arrange the affairs of the world, meaning they descend with its arrangement. The answer to these oaths is omitted, meaning: "You will surely be resurrected, O disbelievers of Makkah." This omitted answer is the ʿāmil (the governing element that determines the case of a word) in "﴿on the Day the quaking one quakes﴾."
﴿On the day the quaker quakes﴾: the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula), by which everything quakes, that is, trembles and is shaken. It is described by what happens as a result of it.

The Second Blast (al-nafkhah al-thaniyah) follows it, and between them are forty years. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to "the Quaking" (al-rajifah). So "the Day" is broad, encompassing both blasts and other things, and thus its being a time-frame (zarfiyyah) for the Resurrection (al-ba'th), which occurs immediately after the Second Blast, is correct.
Hearts on that Day will be trembling (﴿qulūbun yawma'idhin wājifa﴾): fearful and anxious.
﴿Their eyes humbled﴾: abased (dhalilah) by the terror of what they see.

﴿They say﴾, that is, the possessors of hearts and eyes, in mockery and denial of the Resurrection: ﴿Shall we indeed﴾, with the two hamzas (أئنا) pronounced fully, or with the second made easy (تسهيل الثانية), and with an alif inserted between them in both pronunciations, in both places. ﴿Shall we indeed be returned to al-ḥāfirah?﴾ That is: shall we be restored to life after death? Al-ḥāfirah is the name for the first state, the original condition. From it comes the saying, "So-and-so returned in his ḥāfirah," meaning he went back the way he came.
﴿Shall we indeed, when we are bones, decayed?﴾ And in another recitation variant (qira'a), it is read ناخرة (nākhira), meaning: decayed, crumbled into fragments. نَحْيا: we shall be brought to life.

They said, "That, then, would be a losing return." (Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 79:12)

The commentary, as given:

Verse 12 quoted: ﴿They said: That [would be] a return, a losing one.﴾

Gloss: ﴿قالُوا﴾ they said; ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ that, i.e., our returning to life; ﴿إذًا﴾ then, if it is true; ﴿كَرَّة﴾ a return; ﴿خاسِرَة﴾ losing, possessing loss.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 79, verse 13:

﴿Fa-innamā hiya﴾ i.e., the Rādifah (the second blast that is followed by resurrection), ﴿zajrah﴾ a blast, ﴿wāḥidah﴾ a single one. ﴿Fa-idhā nufikhat﴾ (So when it is blown)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 79 (al-Nazi'at), verse 14:

﴿فَإذا هُمْ﴾ (Then, behold, they are) i.e., all of creation ﴿بِالسّاهِرَةِ﴾ (in the sahirah) on the surface of the earth, alive, after they had been dead in its belly.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 15:

﴿Has there come to you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the story of Musa﴾ (operating in "when his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa") —
﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa﴾. The name of the valley is read with tanwin (nunation) and without it, i.e., ﴿طُوًى﴾ and ﴿طُوَى﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 17:

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.﴾ He exceeded the limit in disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 18:

﴿So say: "Would you like to purify yourself?"﴾ I invite you ﴿to purify yourself﴾. In another reading, it is recited with the zay shaddah (تَزَّكّى), with the second tā' assimilated into the zāy, as it was originally: [it means] that you become cleansed of polytheism by testifying that there is no god but Allah.

And I will guide you to your Lord, so that you would fear Him.

Wait, I need to translate the passage faithfully. Here is the translation:

﴿And I will guide you to your Lord﴾ I will show you the way to know Him by proof, ﴿so that you fear Him﴾ so that you fear Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 20:

﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾ from among his nine signs, which were the hand or the staff.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 21:

﴿But he denied﴾ Pharaoh denied Musa, ﴿and disobeyed﴾ Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 22:

﴿Then he turned his back﴾ on faith, ﴿striving﴾ in the land with corruption.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 79, verse 23:

﴿Then he gathered﴾ he assembled the magicians and his soldiers, "and proclaimed."
﴿So he said, "I am your Lord, the Most High."﴾ There is no lord above me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 25:

﴿So Allah seized him﴾ — He destroyed him by drowning — ﴿as an exemplary punishment for the last [utterance] and the first﴾ — i.e., this statement [the last], and the first, i.e., his saying before it: "I do not know of any god for you other than me." Between them was a span of forty years.

Indeed, in that** (the aforementioned matter)** **there is surely a lesson for whoever fears** (Allah, exalted is He).

Translation of the Qur'anic quotation: "Indeed, in that is surely a lesson for whoever fears."

Are you (﴿أأَنَتُّمْ﴾) pronounced with both hamzas fully articulated (tahqiq, meaning pronouncing the hamza in full), with the second changed to an alif, with the second hamza softened (tas'il, meaning easing the hamza), with an alif inserted between the softened hamza and the other, and with that alif omitted? That is, those who deny the resurrection. ﴿Is it harder to create, or the sky?﴾ It is harder to create. ﴿He built it﴾ is an explanation of how it was created.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 28:

﴿He raised its height﴾ is an explanation of the manner of the construction, i.e., He made its elevation high in the direction of the heights. It was said: its height (samk) is its roof. ﴿And made it level﴾: He made it even, without any flaw.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 29:

﴿And He darkened its night﴾, made it dark. ﴿And brought forth its forenoon﴾, made the light of its sun manifest. The night is attributed to it because it is its shadow, and the sun is attributed to it because it is its lamp.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 30:

﴿And after that He spread out the earth﴾ — spread it out (basatha-ha), and it had been created before the heaven without being spread out (min ghayr dahw).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 31:

﴿Akhraja﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), with qad implied before it, meaning: "having brought forth" (mukhrijan) ﴿from it its water﴾ by causing its springs to gush forth, ﴿and its pasture﴾: that which the cattle graze on, namely the trees and herbage, and that which people eat of foodstuffs and fruits. The application of the term "pasture" (mar'ā) to the latter is a metaphor (isti'āra).
﴿And the mountains He set firm﴾ He fixed them on the surface of the earth so that it would be steady.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 33:

﴿Matā‘an﴾ is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose) governed by an implied verb, i.e., He did that as an enjoyment (muta'a), or it is a verbal noun (masdar), i.e., as a giving of enjoyment (tamti'an) ﴿for you and for your cattle﴾. It is the plural of na'am, and it refers to camels, cows and sheep.
﴿فَإذا جاءَتْ الطّامَّة الكُبْرى﴾ "Then when the great catastrophe comes." (Al-Nafkha al-thaniya), the second blast (of the Trumpet).
﴿The Day when man will remember﴾ is a substitution (badal) for ﴿when﴾ (idhā) in the previous verse, ﴿what he strove for﴾ in the world, of good and evil.

﴿And Hellfire was made manifest﴾ [it was made to appear], ﴿the blazing fire﴾ [the burning fire], ﴿for everyone who sees﴾ [for every seer], and the jawab (the response clause of the conditional) of "idha" is: "As for he who transgressed..."
﴿Then as for he who transgressed﴾ disbelieved.
﴿And preferred the worldly life﴾ by following desires.
﴿Then indeed Hellfire is the refuge﴾ his refuge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 40:

﴿And as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ his standing before Him ﴿and restrained the soul﴾ the commanding (al-ammara) soul ﴿from desire﴾ the destructive (al-murdi) desire, by following the appetites.
﴿For indeed, Paradise will be the refuge﴾. The summary of the answer: the disobedient one is in the Fire, and the obedient one is in Paradise.
﴿They ask you﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿about the Hour (al-Sa'ah), when will be its arrival?﴾, meaning: when will its occurrence and its establishment take place?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 43:

﴿Fīma﴾ (about what?) — in what matter? ﴿anta min dhikrāhā﴾ (are you concerned with mentioning it?) — i.e., you do not have knowledge of it, so that you could mention it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 79, verse 44:

﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ Its ultimate knowledge is with none but Him; no one else knows it.
﴿Innama anta mundhir﴾ Your warning benefits only ﴿those who fear it﴾, i.e., who dread it.

As if they had not remained [in their graves] except for an evening or its morning. ﴿As if they had not remained [in their graves] except for an evening or its morning.﴾ That is, an evening of a day or its forenoon. The attribution of the forenoon (ḍuḥā) to the evening was valid because of the close connection between them, since they are the two extremities of the day. What made the attribution acceptable was the occurrence of the concluding word (al-kalima al-fāṣila), which closes the verse.
